# Vānarindajātaka (Ja 57)

**ID:** Ja 57
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)

**Title (Pali):** Vānarindajātaka
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vānarindajātaka* (Ja 57) is a birth story set at the Bamboo Grove (Veḷuvana) near Rājagaha, delivered by the Buddha concerning Devadatta's persistent attempts to kill him [Fausböll 1877]. In the story of the past, the Bodhisatta is born as a monkey-king (*vānarinda*) living along a riverbank who regularly leaps onto a midstream rock to cross to the opposite shore to feed on fruit [Fausböll 1877; War Yar Mein Da 2015]. A crocodile, egged on by his pregnant mate who craves the monkey's heart, lies in wait on the rock disguised as part of the stone [Fausböll 1877; War Yar Mein Da 2015]. Discerning the trap, the monkey tricks the crocodile into opening his mouth—causing the reptile's eyes to close automatically—and leaps swiftly across the crocodile's head to safety [Anandajoti 2010; Fausböll 1877]. Amazed by the monkey's ingenuity, the crocodile utters the canonical verse praising the monkey for possessing four qualities leading to success: truth (*sacca*), virtue (*dhamma*), determination (*dhiti*), and self-sacrifice (*cāga*) (*Yass' ete caturo dhammā vānarinda yathā tava...*) [Anandajoti 2010; Carter 1978; Fausböll 1877]. In the conclusion (*samodhāna*), the crocodile is identified as Devadatta, his wife as Ciñcamāṇavikā, and the clever monkey-king as the Buddha himself [Fausböll 1877].

 DharmaNexus records no Pali-internal or cross-language matches above the similarity threshold [DharmaNexus]. Beyond textual transmission, the story appears in modern adaptations combining related monkey tales (such as Ja 208 and Ja 342) [Appleton 2010], and is historically depicted in early Burmese Buddhist relief sculpture at Pagan [Luce et al. 1970].
